task: reserve a restaurant table online (OpenTable, Resy, Yelp reservations): set party size, date, and time, pick the restaurant, choose an available slot, identify, confirm; complete when the reservation confirmation is on screen. Surface pinned: a reservation website or app. Variants: ordering takeout or delivery, joining a same-day waitlist, and cancelling or modifying an existing reservation do not belong.

tree.label: Reserve a table at a restaurant
tree.note: 1 only when the outing is planned ahead - one keeper (XFZo). then 2, with 3 wherever the engine demands it: before any parameter (BJ-B, rteu), at app start (yW_u), mid-checkout (XFZo's browser round, via 6's plan), or never - the guest form is the whole identity step (N0nZ, NxLJ, dpB7). 4 then 5 on venue routes; 5.1 to 5.4 run before 4 on aggregator routes where party, date, and time are search criteria (DBsq, cJxp, yW_u, dpB7, NxLJ, l-eC, Op82). then 6. 7 once a booking exists - and 7.5 unwinds one (Op82). repeat 4 through 7 per target when the outing takes several tables: XFZo runs the funnel eight times, rteu twice on one venue, hXtq three times without committing. 8 stands alone - 1Jwa runs it before 4 because the balance decides the filter; hXtq and yW_u read it after the bookings.

questions.say_example: The search is set to <2 people, tonight at 7> in <Bologna>. You asked for <4 on Friday> in <Rome>. Fixing it before I search.

questions.question: Does the platform indicate that your party size is too large for online booking and requires calling the restaurant directly?
questions.why: Restaurants often cap online reservations at 6 to 8 people, showing 'no availability' for larger groups even if they actually have space.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user might falsely believe the restaurant is fully booked and give up, instead of making the required phone call to secure a large table.
questions.check: What does the page state as the largest party size bookable online?
questions.say_example: Online booking here stops at <6> people. For your <10>, the page says to call the restaurant. I can't call. That part is yours.

questions.question: What date do you want to set for the reservation?
questions.why: The search bar displays a default date of 'Jul 20, 2023', requiring you to open the calendar to select your actual desired dining day.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose the opportunity to visually review the calendar and pick the date that best fits your schedule.
questions.check: What date does the search bar currently show?
questions.say_example: Set the date to <Friday June 12>, the day you gave me.

questions.question: Does the calendar offer selectable dates beyond the stated last available date?
questions.why: The narrator claims January 4 is the last available date, but the screen shows January 5 as an active, selectable option.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses out on potential booking options if the agent relies on incorrect audio cues rather than the actual on-screen availability.
questions.check: What does the page state as the last available date, and what is the latest date the calendar offers as selectable?
questions.say_example: The page says <January 4> is the last day, but the calendar lets me pick <January 5> too. I'll try it and believe whatever the times list shows.

questions.question: Did the assistant transcribe your party size, date, and time correctly?
questions.why: Verifying the on-screen transcription ensures the voice assistant is searching for the correct party size, date, and time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to instantly catch and correct a voice transcription error before the system retrieves incorrect restaurant options.
questions.check: What party size, date, and time does the on-screen transcription show?
questions.say_example: The screen heard <a table for two on Tuesday>. You said <four on Wednesday>. Fixing it before it searches.

questions.question: Does the times list end in a 'Load More' control, with later slots still hidden behind it?
questions.why: The initial time selection screen only displays afternoon slots up to 5:15 PM, and you must actively click 'Load More' to reveal the later dinner times.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might incorrectly report that the restaurant has no dinner availability if it fails to realize the later times are hidden behind a pagination button.
questions.check: Does the times list end in a Load More control?
questions.say_example: Expanded the times list before concluding anything. The evening slots were behind Load More.

questions.question: Which of the available dinner times do you prefer?
questions.why: The screen lists multiple available dinner slots between 5:00 PM and 10:00 PM, requiring a selection that fits your specific schedule.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to perfectly coordinate the meal time with other specific evening events or personal preferences.
questions.check: Which time slots does the page list as available?
questions.say_example: Your <7 pm> was there, so I took it.

questions.question: Which alternative timeslot should you pick since your time isn't available?
questions.why: The screen showed that the requested 7:00 PM slot was unavailable, requiring a choice between the available 5:00 PM, 8:00 PM, or 8:15 PM options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to weigh your personal schedule flexibility to decide whether eating significantly earlier or later is better for your plans.
questions.check: Which time slots does the page list as available, and is the requested time among them?
questions.say_example: No <7 pm> left. There's <5>, <8>, and <8:15>. I can also join the waitlist or watch for a cancellation. Which do you want?

children.label: Trade the discount against the time

questions.question: Which available seating option do you prefer?
questions.why: The screen prompts you to select a seating option, showing that Standard and Outdoor are available while High top is marked unavailable.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to choose your preferred dining atmosphere, such as opting to sit indoors rather than outdoors.
questions.check: Which seating options does the page list as available and unavailable?
questions.say_example: No standard tables at that time, only <outdoor> and <bar> seats. Which is fine for you?

questions.question: If you selected outdoor seating, does the restaurant guarantee an indoor table if it rains, or will the reservation be cancelled?
questions.why: Many restaurants do not have backup indoor space for patio reservations, meaning bad weather could ruin the dining plans.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to check the weather policy and decide if the risk of a cancelled meal is acceptable.
questions.check: What does the page state happens to outdoor reservations in bad weather?
questions.say_example: The page says patio bookings <aren't moved inside if it rains>. Bad weather and the table is gone.

questions.question: Does the selected time slot have a visual icon, such as an umbrella or barstool, indicating a non-standard seating area?
questions.why: Platforms often use small visual icons instead of text labels to indicate that a specific time slot is for outdoor, high-top, or bar seating.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user might arrive expecting a standard dining room table but be seated outside in poor weather or at the bar because they could not see the visual-only cue.
questions.check: Does the selected slot carry a seating label other than standard?
questions.say_example: That <7:15> slot has a little <umbrella> mark. It's an outdoor table, not a regular one.

questions.question: Which of the conflicting reservations do you want to keep?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Conflicting Reservations' modal warning that keeping the new reservation will automatically cancel the existing one.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide which reservation is more important to keep when a scheduling conflict occurs.
questions.check: What does the conflict warning say happens to the existing reservation if this one is kept?
questions.say_example: Booking this cancels your <existing 6 pm> reservation. The site won't keep both. Keep the old one, or swap it for this?

children.note: 6.1 with 6.2 against it. 6.3 wherever a field is empty - the phone number is the one hard gate in this corpus. 6.4 to 6.6 as the form offers them; 6.7 and 6.8 where policies, fees, or entitlements ride the booking; then 6.9 and 6.10. the whole goal runs against a countdown on three engines (XFZo 10 minutes, rteu from 10, l-eC 4:49, NxLJ 5:00). XFZo's browser round reaches back into 3.4 when the password wall lands here. hXtq stops at the button on purpose, three times; N0nZ and s4oX end before it; l-eC ends on its spinner.

questions.question: Who should I select from your saved contacts for the other three guests?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify exactly which family members or friends are attending the reservation.

questions.question: What phone number and special requests do you want to include?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify their preferred contact number and communicate any specific needs or preferences to the restaurant.
questions.check: Which contact fields does the form show, and which are already filled?
questions.say_example: I'm putting in your name and <mobile> number now. You didn't ask for any special requests, so that stays blank.

questions.question: Do you need to add any dietary restrictions, accessibility requests, or celebration cakes?
questions.why: The screen offered options to add a Mickey Mouse Celebration Cake, dietary requests, or accessibility requests to the reservation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to customize the dining experience with special cakes or ensure your dietary and accessibility needs are accommodated.
questions.check: Which request fields — dietary, accessibility, add-ons — does the form offer?

questions.question: Did an error message appear stating that the selected time slot was taken by someone else while you were filling out the details?
questions.why: Reservation systems do not always hold a table while you type, and highly sought-after slots can be booked by another user simultaneously.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to immediately select an alternative time before the remaining slots are also gone.
questions.check: Does the page show an error saying the selected time is no longer available?
questions.say_example: Someone took that table while we were filling the form. I'm back at the times list, and <8:15> is still open.

questions.question: How much time is currently remaining on the visual hold timer?
questions.why: Reservation systems often hold the table for a strict window, displaying a ticking visual timer that dictates how fast the user must provide their details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness of urgency and might take too long deciding on special requests or finding their credit card, causing the table to be released.
questions.check: What does the hold timer on the page show?
questions.say_example: The form had a <5-minute> hold timer. That was plenty of time.

questions.question: Are the reservation details in the summary correct before you proceed?
questions.why: The screen displays a reservation summary with the restaurant name, date, and time, which must be verified before clicking Next.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify the exact reservation details before the agent proceeds to finalize the booking.
questions.check: What restaurant, date, time, and party size does the summary show?
questions.say_example: The summary says <Saturday> at <7:15> for <2>. You asked for <Friday> at <7> for <4>. Fixing it before we go on.

children.label: Check the booking against the request

questions.question: Are the dates and party sizes consistent across all steps of your planning and booking?
questions.why: The dining plan calculator shown earlier was configured for a trip in March 2026 for 1 adult, but the actual reservations are for April 2026 for 2 guests.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the reservations are being made for the correct trip dates and party size.
questions.check: What dates and party sizes do the planning page and the booking page each show?
questions.say_example: Your planner was set up for <March, 1 adult>, but this booking says <April, 2 guests>. One of them is off. Which is right?

questions.question: Does the phone number on the booking page match the official restaurant website?
questions.why: The Universal Orlando website and the Zomato booking page displayed different phone numbers for Antojitos, suggesting a possible mismatch in the location.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to catch conflicting contact details that might indicate a reservation is being made at the wrong location.
questions.check: What phone number does the booking page show, and what number does the restaurant's own site show?
questions.say_example: The phone number on this booking page doesn't match the restaurant's own site. This might be a different location, or a stale listing. Let me check before booking.

questions.question: Do the available time slots on the restaurant's detail page match the ones shown in the search results?
questions.why: The search results displayed one set of available times, but the restaurant's detail page offered a different and expanded list of options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to select a more convenient time slot that was only revealed after clicking through to the restaurant's detail page.
questions.check: Which times does the search result card list, and which does the detail page list?
questions.say_example: The detail page showed more times than the search card. I went by the detail page.

questions.question: A red 'first name is required' error is blocking the reservation - take over the field and enter it?
questions.why: The screen displays a red error message stating the first name is required, which will prevent the reservation from being completed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure your personal details are correctly entered to successfully secure the booking.
questions.check: Does the page show a required-field error on the name?
questions.say_example: The form flagged the empty name field. I filled it and moved on.

questions.question: Is the form pre-filled with the right person's contact details?
questions.why: The narrator instructs you to enter your name, phone number, and email, but the screen shows these fields are already filled with Sophia Cruz's details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the agent can recognize when a form is already auto-filled and avoid redundant data entry.
questions.check: What name, phone, and email does the form show pre-filled?
questions.say_example: The form came pre-filled for <Sophia Cruz>. That's not you. I'm replacing it with your details.

questions.question: Is the reservation being booked under the name of the person who will actually be arriving at the restaurant?
questions.why: The form often auto-fills with the account holder's name, but if you are booking on behalf of someone else, the restaurant needs the actual diner's name to seat them.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks the actual diner being turned away or delayed if the agent books the table under the account holder's name instead.
questions.check: What name does the booking form show?
questions.say_example: The form put the booking under <your> name, but <your mom> is the one going. The restaurant seats by the name on the booking. Book it under hers?

questions.question: Did the form reject your phone number because it requires a mobile number or a specific country code format?
questions.why: The phone input field specifies 'Mobile Only' and includes a country code selector, meaning an incorrectly formatted number or a landline will trigger a validation error and block the reservation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might get stuck on a validation error if it tries to input a landline or a number without the correct country code, failing to complete the booking.
questions.check: Does the page show a validation error on the phone field, and what does it say is required?
questions.say_example: The form won't take that number. It wants a mobile with a country code. Is there a mobile I should use instead?

questions.question: Do you want to pre-order any food items for this reservation?
questions.why: The screen presents optional add-on food items like charcuterie boards and olives that can be purchased before finalizing the booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to purchase specific snacks in advance or rely on complimentary food options.
questions.check: Which optional add-on items does the page offer, and at what prices?
questions.say_example: Skipped the add-ons (<charcuterie board>, <olives>). You didn't ask for them.

questions.question: Do you want to opt in to promotional emails and text updates before completing the reservation?
questions.why: The screen presents checkboxes for receiving dining offers, news, and text updates that must be decided on before clicking the complete reservation button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to control whether your contact information is used for marketing emails and text message reminders.
questions.check: Which marketing checkboxes does the page show, and are any pre-ticked?
questions.say_example: Said no to marketing emails and texts. Kept the booking-confirmation messages on.

questions.question: What are the restaurant's specific dining policies?
questions.why: The screen displays important dining information like a 15-minute grace period, party size limits, and age restrictions that you need to know before going.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss seeing crucial restrictions or fees, such as a strict grace period or a cake fee, that could negatively impact your dining experience.
questions.check: What policies does the page state — grace period, party limits, age rules?
questions.say_example: They hold the table <15 minutes> past your time, then release it.

questions.question: What is the exact deadline to cancel this reservation without being charged the penalty fee?
questions.why: The guest policies state a specific timeframe (like 24 hours or 2 hours prior) by which the reservation must be cancelled to avoid the per-person credit card guarantee fee.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the critical knowledge of how long they have to change their mind or adjust their plans without suffering a financial penalty.
questions.check: What does the policy text state about charges: how much, charged when or only held, and free cancellation until when?
questions.say_example: You can cancel free until <Friday 7 pm>. After that they charge <$10> a person. That's <$40> for the four of you.

questions.question: Does the booking policy state a strict time limit for your table, such as 90 minutes or 2 hours?
questions.why: Many restaurants enforce dining duration limits during peak hours, which might not suit a long, leisurely celebration.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to realize their meal will be rushed and decide to book elsewhere for a more relaxed experience.
questions.check: Does the policy text state a table time limit?
questions.say_example: The table is yours for <90 minutes>. It's in their policy.

questions.question: Is your club member discount correctly applied to the final price?
questions.why: The order summary lists a $10 club discount, so you must verify it is actually deducted from the $65 subtotal before paying.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying that your membership perks are correctly reducing the final cost.
questions.check: What discount line does the summary show, and what is the total?
questions.say_example: The page shows your <$10 club discount>, but the total still reads <$65>. It wasn't taken off. I'm not going ahead until the math is right.

questions.question: Does the discount actually apply to this booking, and what does it exclude?
questions.why: A blue banner explicitly states 'Esta reserva não inclui ofertas' (This reservation does not include offers), alerting you that the specific time you picked does not qualify for the expected discount.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might complete a full-price booking, failing to catch that the selected time slot silently dropped the promotional discount.
questions.check: Does the summary show a notice that offers don't apply, or state what the discount excludes?
questions.say_example: Heads up, the page says this slot doesn't include the offers. The <30% off> you saw won't apply to this booking.

questions.question: Are you ready to accept the terms and submit the reservation?
questions.why: Tapping the reserve button finalizes the booking and constitutes your agreement to receive text messages and accept Yelp's terms of service and privacy policy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to read and evaluate the terms of service and privacy policy before legally consenting to them.
questions.check: What restaurant, date, time, party size, name, card, and cancellation terms does the final page show?
questions.say_example: Ready to book. <The Zen Bistro>, <Friday June 12> at <7>, table for <4>, under <your name>. They'll hold your <Visa ending 4821>. There's no charge unless you don't show, then <$40>. Free to cancel until <Thursday>. Press to book, or say change.

questions.question: Did you complete the reservation before the hold timer expired?
questions.why: The screen shows a five-minute hold timer, but the recording ends before the reservation is actually finalized.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the guarantee of a reserved table because the booking process was never fully completed.
questions.check: Does the page show the hold expired or the slot released?
questions.say_example: The hold ran out while we filled the form. The table went back to everyone. <8:15> still shows. Grab it?

children.note: 7.1, then 7.2 where the platform offers next steps. 7.3 on email engines; 7.4 closes the loop in the account. 7.5 unwinds a booking entirely - Op82 only; XFZo never needs it because 5.10 auto-cancelled the old ones.

questions.question: Are the confirmed reservation details correct?
questions.why: Seeing the green checkmark and "Booking Confirmed" message alongside the specific date, time, and party size ensures the reservation was successfully processed exactly as requested.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss the immediate peace of mind of verifying the final booking details yourself and the chance to instantly use the on-screen options to invite your guests.

questions.question: Does the confirmation screen indicate that you have a guaranteed table, or have you merely been added to a standby waitlist?
questions.why: Some platforms allow you to join a waitlist when reservations are full, which does not guarantee a specific dining time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user might arrive at the restaurant expecting immediate seating, only to discover they are on a waitlist and face a long delay.
questions.check: Does the confirmation say booked, or waitlist?
questions.say_example: This isn't a booked table. The confirmation says standby waitlist. You'd only get seats if someone cancels. Want me to keep hunting for a real table?

questions.question: Does the confirmation screen state that the reservation is 'pending' or 'awaiting restaurant approval'?
questions.why: Some smaller or exclusive restaurants manually review bookings before confirming, meaning the table is not guaranteed immediately.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user might mistakenly assume their plans are set and fail to check back for the actual approval or book a backup.
questions.check: Does the confirmation say pending or awaiting approval?
questions.say_example: The booking is pending. The restaurant still has to approve it. Not guaranteed yet. I'll watch for their answer.

questions.question: Do you want to modify or cancel this booking using the links in the confirmation email?
questions.why: The confirmation email displays your final booking details alongside buttons to immediately modify or cancel the reservation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the emailed booking details and immediately use the provided links to make changes if your plans shifted.
questions.check: Does the confirmation email show modify and cancel links?
questions.say_example: The confirmation email has the change and cancel links. Cancelling stays free until <Thursday>.

questions.question: If the booking screen hangs on a loading spinner, did you receive a confirmation email to prove the reservation actually succeeded?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might assume the booking failed and try to book again, accidentally creating a duplicate reservation, or assume it succeeded when it actually dropped.
questions.check: Does the page show a confirmed state, and does a confirmation email exist for this booking?
